title: st attach --from over an existing attachment says ok and changes nothing while intentd watches the tree
body:
Observed twice on 2026-11-19 with brew 3.4.0 (vc), in this repository's main checkout, while the brew intentd answered at `~/.local/state/intent/run/intentd.sock` and watched the tree.

- `intent st attach ST0095 design.md --from <new file>` and `intent st attach ST0096 design.md --from <new file>`, each over an attachment the thread already held and whose realised `intent/st/<ID>/design.md` was on disk, printed `ok: design.md written to <ID>`. The ST0095 attach also printed `wrote:` for the thread's canon.
- Afterwards each thread's canon held the old text, and each realised `design.md` still held the old bytes. The next verb that wrote ST0095's canon (`intent set` on a work package's body) warned "overwrote bytes that were not the store's render -- an edit to a generated file is gone" and named the canon file.
- Copying the new text over the realised file instead was taken in by the daemon at once, and the canon's attachment then matched the file by sha256 and bytes.
- The same happened in the morning: a re-attach did not reach the realised file, and the edit went in through the file on disk.

Read, not confirmed: the realised file is an attachment's authoring surface, so the watching daemon may have taken in the old file on disk over what the attach had just written. Either way the verb said `ok` and the change did not stand, which No Silent Errors forbids.

Expected: `st attach --from` over an existing attachment either replaces it in the store, the canon and the realised file together, or refuses with the route that works: edit the realised file, or stop the daemon first.
